clue.text: Confront some of those on the staff

definitions.meaning: to confront someone is to meet them head-on

definitions.text: some of those on the staff
definitions.meaning: the notes in the spaces of the treble staff in music spell out this word, the mnemonic every piano pupil learns

explanation.surface: An order to stand up to some of one's colleagues at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but is the musical stave: the four spaces of the treble clef hold the notes F, A, C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting a challenge head-on is facing it; the musical notes are a classic mnemonic.

clue.text: Dash, following American spies

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of spies

explanation.surface: A quick scramble after US intelligence agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' is short for dashboard, the instrument panel of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The panel in front of a driver is the dashboard, also called by this name in British usage.

clue.text: Ordered, new director (education)

parts.note: the printed punctuation mark after the first word is itself a piece of the wordplay, named for what it is

explanation.surface: A school appointment announced: a fresh head has been installed in education.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation mark right after 'Ordered' is itself part of the wordplay: the printed comma supplies the opening letters, before N, D and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ordered is to have been given a command, so the past tense of the verb fits.

clue.text: As whistleblower, caution Zuck finally following expression of contempt

indicators.note: following tells us the next piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: a boo is a jeer of contempt from a crowd

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the name Zuck

explanation.surface: A whistleblower speaks out against Mark Zuckerberg amid public scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As whistleblower' sets up the football sense: a referee blows the whistle, then cautions a player by writing their name down. Zuck is Mark Zuckerberg, the Facebook boss, completing the theme with 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a referee who cautions a player shows a yellow card and records the offence in a notebook.

clue.text: Plod's wrinkly pecker?

definitions.note: read as 'Plod is'; Mr Plod, the policeman in Enid Blyton's Noddy stories, is British slang for the police

parts.note: a wrinkly is slang for an old person, and as an adjective means aged
a pecker is a bird's beak, also called its bill

explanation.surface: A rude joke about a policeman's ageing anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pecker' tempts a rude reading but it is a beak. Plod and this answer are both British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang names for the police force, the answer being the older London term.

clue.text: Docking fee upset European nerd going round Alabama

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the whole string is turned upside down, read from the bottom
going round says the word for nerd surrounds the state abbreviation

parts.note: a geek is a nerd, an obsessive
AL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Alabama

explanation.surface: A port charge annoys a European nerd travelling through the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' wraps the nerd around the state; 'upset' then turns the whole string, E included, over so it reads from the bottom up, giving EGALEEK backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The charge a ship pays to stay in a harbour or dock is named after its keel.

clue.text: Indicator watched by Wall Street and the soup kitchen?

definitions.text: Indicator watched by Wall Street and the soup kitchen?

parts.words: Indicator watched by Wall Street and the soup kitchen?
parts.note: traders follow the value of company shares, while a soup kitchen would care what it costs to buy broth base, a second sense of the first word

explanation.surface: A market measure followed both by financiers and by a charity kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word means both company shares and the broth base soup is made from, so one figure serves both watchers.
explanation.definitionFit: The value at which shares trade is the market measure investors track, and the cost of broth matters to a kitchen.

clue.text: Pastures new for Republican big beast?

indicators.note: new says the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A senior Republican figure moving on to fresh territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pastures new' is a stock phrase for a change of job, but 'new' is the anagram signal on PASTURES plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A big beast is a dominant figure in politics or any field, a celebrity of great stature.

clue.text: One trapped between legs? It could make your eyes water!

definitions.text: It could make your eyes water!

indicators.note: trapped between says the numeral sits caught in the middle of the two other pieces

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so two legs give ON twice
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wince-inducing image of something caught between the thighs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a painful blow, but 'legs' is the cricket term: the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping this vegetable releases a compound that stings the eyes and brings tears.

clue.text: Guard to look over Buddhist temple children

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read from the bottom up in this down clue

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look
a wat is a Buddhist temple or monastery in Thailand or Cambodia

explanation.surface: A guard is told to watch over children at a Buddhist temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like part of 'look over' but turns PEEK into KEEP. A wat is a temple in Thailand or Cambodia.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard something is to stand vigilant over it, observing and protecting.

clue.text: Bess's partner's topless romp

indicators.note: topless means the first letter, the top in a down clue, is taken away

parts.note: Porgy is the partner of Bess in Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about a racy encounter with nothing above the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' seems to belong to the racy picture, but it removes the first letter of PORGY.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild romp is a debauched party, so the two are close in meaning.

clue.text: Caught by digital camera, an iffy Trump lobbyist?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: iffy means dubious or unsound, so these letters are put in a questionable new order

explanation.surface: A shady pro-Trump operative gets snapped on a hidden digital camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' seems to link C to the camera, but its letters join DIGITAL CAMERA AN as the anagram fodder. The firm's boss was secretly filmed by Channel 4 in 2018.
explanation.definitionFit: The data firm worked for the Trump campaign, so it could be called, with a question mark, a lobbyist for him.

clue.text: See 6
Shelter for naval ships getting shelled

indicators.note: getting shelled means the outer letters are stripped away like a shell

parts.note: a fleet is a body of naval ships

explanation.surface: Warships come under fire from shells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' looks like bombardment but means the outer casing is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The side sheltered from the wind, as in the lee of a hill, is a place of shelter.

clue.text: See 10
Setback for Wenger as head of Gunners fails to extend contract

indicators.note: fails means that letter goes missing from the string
setback for says the name is set back, written from right to left
head of picks out the opening letter of Gunners

explanation.surface: Arsene Wenger, Arsenal's manager, suffers a blow when his club fails to give him a new deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal are nicknamed the Gunners and Wenger was their long-serving manager. 'Setback for' turns WENGER into REGNEW; 'fails' removes the G.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend a contract is to prolong it for a further term.

clue.text: A little nephew I'd throw across the swimming pool

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An uncle boasts about tossing a small nephew from side to side of a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimmers measure laps as lengths or the shorter distance across the pool from side to side.

clue.text: The big picture as seen from the space station?

definitions.text: The big picture as seen from the space station?

parts.words: The big picture as seen from the space station?
parts.note: a broad outlook on life is the big picture, and from orbit you literally see the whole planet

explanation.surface: What astronauts see from orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally: the view of the planet from space.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosophy of life is a big-picture outlook, and from orbit one sees the globe whole.

clue.text: Upsetting party, Powell (ex-Conservative) involved in dirty tricks campaign

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting means the whole string is turned upside down
ex says the following element is dropped, as in a former member

parts.note: Enoch Powell was a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: An upsetting party with the ex-Tory Enoch Powell caught up in a smear campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ex' removes C from ENOCH to leave ENOH; 'Upsetting' turns PARTY plus ENOH over. Cambridge Analytica's boss was filmed discussing such schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme using sexual entrapment to compromise someone is a classic dirty trick.

clue.text: Ordered earliest time to be in repose

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A doctor's instruction for an early bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like an instruction, but it rearranges EARLIEST with T.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to rest peacefully, used particularly of the dead lying in their grave.

clue.text: Fashionable new bar

parts.note: something in is fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy watering hole has just opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or tavern is a place with a bar serving drinks.

clue.text: Gregarious Nix at last caught by film, right on time

indicators.note: caught by says the letter is held inside the film's title

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial

indicators.note: at last points at the closing letter of Nix

parts.note: on and over both mean about, concerning, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: Alexander Nix, the Cambridge Analytica boss, is finally caught on film.
explanation.walkthrough: Nix was secretly filmed by Channel 4 talking about his firm's methods.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociable, outgoing person who enjoys company is the opposite of an introvert.

clue.text: Shoot Nad nude, rolling around and around having nothing on

indicators.note: the second around turns that string round so it is read from right to left
around says the letters lie about within the run of words before it, spread across them

explanation.surface: A tabloid story about a politician called Nad being photographed naked and rolling about.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards from the last letter of 'Shoot' through 'Nad nude' to the first of 'rolling'. 'Nude' and 'nothing on' both suggest nakedness, but the definition means out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone laid off from their job has no work, nothing on their schedule.

clue.text: Dead-beat loyalist political party did their sums

indicators.note: beat means the letters before it are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party, a Northern Ireland loyalist party

explanation.surface: A down-and-out unionist party has done its accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead-beat' reads as one word, but 'beat' is the anagram signal on DEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To total figures is to calculate them, which is what doing sums means.

clue.text: Mo, 3, worked out maths formula

indicators.note: worked out says these letters are rearranged into the solution

parts.note: the numeral 3 is spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: A pupil named Mo, aged three, solves an equation.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 3 is spelt out as THREE, joining MO as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition proved by reasoning, like Pythagoras', is a mathematical statement.

clue.text: Gag on tandoori chicken hot starters

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: starters picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Choking on a curry-house appetiser that is too spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' fits the meal but takes initial letters of 'tandoori chicken hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to heave as if about to vomit.

clue.text: I'd teach doddery President about grubby tricks for budget problem solving

definitions.text: grubby tricks for budget problem solving

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved round into a different order

explanation.surface: An old president is given lessons in shady schemes to fix a budget crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: All 23 letters of 'I'd teach doddery President' are rearranged, signalled by 'about'. The phrase is an AC/DC song title, apt for the Cambridge Analytica theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby tricks are dirty deeds, and doing them for a budget price means cheaply.

clue.text: Extolled unlimited pay increase

indicators.note: unlimited means the outer letters, the limits, are taken off

parts.note: to extol is to praise highly

explanation.surface: A generous pay rise was praised to the skies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' looks like an endless pay rise but trims the ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase in wages is known as a rise, or in American usage this word.

clue.text: See 24
Fire rifle

definitions.meaning: to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job
to rifle through something is to ransack or plunder it

explanation.definitionFit: Dismissing staff is giving them the push, and plundering a town is pillaging.

clue.text: Vacate space for Australian company

parts.note: an em is a printer's space, the width of the letter M
Pty is the abbreviation for proprietary, used in Australian company names such as Pty Ltd

explanation.surface: Instructions to clear out office space for a company from Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: Pty Ltd is the Australian equivalent of a limited company.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacate a room is to clear it out, leaving nothing in it.

clue.text: Occasionally stroked David Mellor's erogenous zone, allegedly

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A dig at a scandal-hit politician's alleged fondness for being stroked.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1992 the tabloids claimed Tory minister David Mellor enjoyed having his feet sucked in a Chelsea shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The tabloid story claimed his digits on the foot were the minister's sensitive spot.

clue.text: Here in Versailles, her majesty is more frigid

parts.note: ici is French for here, and Versailles is in France
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen on a visit to the French palace, frostier than ever.
explanation.walkthrough: ER = Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Colder, more frosty in temperature or manner.

clue.text: See 24
Midwife essentially is to assist to give birth

indicators.note: essentially picks the central letter, the essence, of Midwife

parts.note: to help is to assist

explanation.surface: A midwife's essential job is to assist women in labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' reads as 'basically' but takes the centre of MIDWIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is used of dogs and other animals producing young.

clue.text: Cougar getting stuck into the spumante?

indicators.note: getting stuck into says the answer lies embedded inside the next word

explanation.surface: An older woman enjoying a bottle of Italian sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cougar' is slang for an older woman, but here it is the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The American big cat is also called a mountain lion; both names are the same animal.

clue.text: Support "Remain"

definitions.meaning: a prop or brace, such as a rope steadying a mast
to remain is to stick around or not leave

explanation.surface: A Brexit campaign slogan backing the side that wanted to keep Britain in the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace holding up a mast is called by this name, and not leaving is the verb's sense.
